title: Punt TO: Player Targets
markdown:
**Summary.** Punting turnovers costs us little in 9-cat head-to-head. Every first-round star turns the ball over, and streaming for games adds turnovers anyway. Build around high-usage scorers and passers, pay market price only for true anchors, and get the most profit from mid-round guards and forwards whose site prices sit below the expert view.

## Why experts ignore turnovers

Three expert sources ignore turnovers in head-to-head leagues. Lloyd ignores them in every head-to-head league, and another speaker ignores them completely. The reason is simple. Turnovers are a third of the usage formula, so every first-round player has high turnovers. If you draft high-usage, high-value players, you cannot avoid them. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=549), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1857), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2141), [09-17](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=303))

For our auction this means one thing. If you plan to spend big on an anchor such as Jokić, Wembanyama or Dončić, you already carry a turnover cost. Accept it before 2026-10-18 and stop letting turnovers lower your bids on high-usage players. Each week you then aim to win at least five of the other eight categories. ([09-17](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=303), [09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2141), [Nikola Jokić](#player/288), [Victor Wembanyama](#player/591), [Luka Dončić](#player/147))

## Streaming raises turnovers anyway

Turnovers are the only negative counting stat in the format. Streaming to get the most games played raises turnovers by itself. Chasing low turnovers therefore fights the way head-to-head is won. In our league that means using daily lineups and the 6 weekly acquisitions to add games, without worrying about the turnovers the extra games bring. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=2119), [09-14](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=813))

The reverse also holds. Injuries and light schedules lower your turnovers automatically. So in weeks when you are short on games, you often win turnovers anyway. Do not plan for that category. Just take the win when it comes. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=2208))

Check which rankings you use. One expert's head-to-head system pushes centers down. In head-to-head, low turnovers matter less because you want the most games played. He also says traditional box-score values overrate blocks, steals and some percentages. A list that rewards low turnovers will undervalue the high-usage players we want. ([09-14](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=813))

## What you give up and what you gain

Watch how categories move together. High assists go with high turnovers. Low turnovers go with low points and assists. Punting turnovers lets you buy assist-heavy guards and point forwards at full value. A team built to win turnovers ends up giving away points and assists too. High blocks go with high rebounds and FG%, so a big-man core can sit alongside a punt TO build. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=588))

Turnovers still have one use. If two players are otherwise identical at the same price, pick the one with fewer turnovers. ([07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=2232))

The notes do not disagree on the main point, but they differ in degree. Lloyd and one speaker ignore turnovers completely in head-to-head. Another expert says only that low turnovers matter less, and the speaker who ignores them still uses them as a tiebreaker. Our rule: never pay extra for low turnovers, but use them to decide between equal options. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=549), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1857), [07-15](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=2232), [09-14](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=813))

## Price tiers for our auction

Every player on this list carries the punt TO fit tag. The fit is common, so it is not a reason to overbid. It adds value only at a sensible price. Core anchors are the first-round stars whose only weak category is turnovers. Pay the market for them, but stop at the caps in their notes. For Wembanyama, the extra cost above about 75 USD comes out of the rest of the roster. Do not chase Cunningham past the mid 50s. ([Victor Wembanyama](#player/591), [Cade Cunningham](#player/123), [Jayson Tatum](#player/543), [Anthony Edwards](#player/160), [Giannis Antetokounmpo](#player/19))

The middle tier is where the price is the key decision. The sites price Jalen Johnson as a first-rounder, but experts see him in the mid second round. Towns is going too high above about 40 USD. Last season our league paid points-league money for Booker, Harden and Banchero. Bid on these players only when the price matches the expert rank. ([Jalen Johnson](#player/280), [Karl-Anthony Towns](#player/560), [Devin Booker](#player/51), [James Harden](#player/219), [Paolo Banchero](#player/29))

The best profit is in guards and forwards whose site costs sit below the expert view. These include Dejounte Murray, Garland, Keyonte George, Brandon Miller, Jaren Jackson Jr., Boozer and Edey. Check Miller's shoulder in training camp before the 2026-10-18 auction, and check that Edey's ankle tag has cleared. ([Dejounte Murray](#player/399), [Darius Garland](#player/185), [Keyonte George](#player/187), [Brandon Miller](#player/381), [Jaren Jackson Jr.](#player/265), [Cameron Boozer](#player/52), [Zach Edey](#player/158))

With 144 players drafted, the last roster spots go to flyers for a few USD. These are Morant, Queen, Jalen Green and Dybantsa for points and assists. Ingram is an Achilles stash for one of our 4 IL slots. ([Ja Morant](#player/397), [Derik Queen](#player/466), [Jalen Green](#player/208), [AJ Dybantsa](#player/155), [Brandon Ingram](#player/257))

## Playoff schedule and early checks

Our playoffs are weeks 19 to 21, ending 2027-03-28. Edwards has a two-game week 20. Mitchell and Harden have a two-game finals week. LaMelo Ball has a two-game playoff week. Durant and Sengun get only 10 playoff games, so think about trading them before the 2027-03-04 deadline. Flagg's 4-4-4 schedule and the Clippers' 4-3-4 add value. Philadelphia has three back-to-backs in our playoff weeks, so keep a backup ready behind Embiid and LeBron. The finals-week worry for Dejounte Murray applies only to an April 4 end, so it does not affect us. ([Anthony Edwards](#player/160), [Donovan Mitchell](#player/391), [James Harden](#player/219), [LaMelo Ball](#player/27), [Kevin Durant](#player/153), [Alperen Sengun](#player/502), [Cooper Flagg](#player/174), [Brandon Ingram](#player/257), [Darius Garland](#player/185), [Joel Embiid](#player/165), [LeBron James](#player/269), [Dejounte Murray](#player/399))

Early in the season, check assists and usage on your punt TO core first, because those are the stats that come with the turnovers. Check whether Jokić's assists hold near 10, whether Dončić's move toward nine, whether Cunningham's climb past 10 and whether Giannis's rise in Miami. If the assists do not arrive, you are taking the turnovers without the payoff. ([09-23](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=588), [Nikola Jokić](#player/288), [Luka Dončić](#player/147), [Cade Cunningham](#player/123), [Giannis Antetokounmpo](#player/19))
